Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=x+6,$ $y=2x,$ and $y=3x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2} \\ y=x+6 & \,⟹\,x=y-6 \\ y=3x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070962/assets/c453d46a1f0cd6e6ddfa926de471fe38663df2bd86b9cdf4e58ce8d42462774a.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 9,\,\frac{y}{3}\le x\le \frac{y}{2}}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,y)\,:\,9\le y\le 12,\,y-6\le x\le \frac{y}{2}}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{9}{\int }_{y/3}^{y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{9}^{12}{\int }_{y-6}^{y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
